items.title: Al Wynn Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: So I worked with Jimmy until that fall. We were on WBBM there, broadcasting. And it was, he had a big band there.

ctx.x: Well, we got the end of that story. And that's just something else that you think ought to be told, especially?

Well, there's nothing other than that when I come to Chicago. Nothing very much was happening here. I went with Jesse Stone. We finally got a band together and opened a new spot here, the Club Morocco. But they had a lot of hometown boys that didn't want to go any place. It was discontented. Never the type of Jimmy Noon now. Yeah, Jimmy Noon eventually went in the same place. So, uh, in the meantime, I leave Jimmy Stone and go with Carol Dixon as a replacement at the Grand Terrace when Earl would go out on the…

items.title: Eurreal Wilford "Little Brother" Montgomery Interview, 1958-05-29
items.q: But when I first come back from Europe I worked with Jimmy in I guess it would be early 33. He got a band together, a new spot open, a very beautiful place on 55th Street, Club Morocco.

ctx.x: Was that still the district up there?

That was the district. That was the last. That was the last. The district was fading, but there still was a slight resemblance of it. I mean Bloom, the name of Artie Bloom I think still had the Frolics there. And well of course they had terrific shows and they had big shows. Ralph Edwards had the house band there. So they wanted a band just to play at animation time. So what happened, this, before then they had a lot of flow entertainers, you know, with the small pianos and the girl singers. They would push them…

Preston. So Preston made the record. Are there any other records that you might be on that maybe people don't know about? Of course you don't know what people know but I mean the ones you made under your own name and say the Ma Rainey? And can you think of anything else now that people might not have heard about?
